hook.text: Jakarta sinks 10 inches per year. Parts of the city are already 13 feet below sea level. Ten million people live there.

buildup.text: Unregulated groundwater pumping is the cause. Buildings sit on water-logged soil that compresses as water is extracted.

discovery.text: Rising seas from climate change make it worse. By 2050, a third of Jakarta could be permanently underwater.

twist.text: Indonesia is moving its capital to Nusantara on Borneo — abandoning Jakarta rather than saving it.

climax.text: The new capital will cost $35 billion. Critics ask: who saves the 10 million people left behind?

punchline.text: The capital is sinking. So the government is leaving.

quiz.question: Why is Jakarta sinking?
options: Tectonic plate movement beneath the city
Unregulated groundwater pumping compresses the soil
Rising sea levels from climate change are the sole cause
